title: Finite projective dimension of the residue field is bounded by depth
statement: Let R be a Noetherian local ring with residue field kappa. If kappa has finite projective dimension over R (def-weil-pbc-finite-global-dimension), then pd_R kappa is at most depth of R as a module over itself (def-weil-pbc-depth).

proof.text: Use the bounded-resolution/Ext-dimension bridge [lem-weil-pbc-projective-resolution-ext-degree] to turn finite categorical projective dimension into existence of a bounded projective resolution. Let d be Nat.find of this existence. Nat.find_spec supplies its resolution. If d=0, nonnegativity of depth suffices; otherwise apply the minimal finite free resolution theorem to the finite residue-field module.

Choose finite bases for the free terms [def-weil-pbc-free-module], reindexed by Fin(n_i). The rank n_d is nonzero: if it vanished then P_d would be a zero object, so the same projective resolution P would have zero terms in all degrees greater than d-1. Nat.find_min' for the defining minimum [def-weil-pbc-finite-global-dimension] would imply d <= d-1, contrary to d >= 1. This avoids choosing a largest nonzero index or constructing a truncated resolution.

Conjugate each differential P_i -> P_(i-1) by the basis coordinate equivalences and take its matrix phi_i with LinearMap.toMatrix'. Transport the positive-degree exactness of P [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence] through these equivalences: a vector in the kernel has a preimage in P_(i+1), whose coordinates give its matrix preimage. Since P_(d+1) is zero, exactness at P_d makes the last differential injective. Thus the matrices satisfy the complex, exactness, and injectivity hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-exact-free-complex-last-minors-regular-sequence].

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-free-complex-last-minors-regular-sequence] with e=d. Its last-minor ideal I is either the whole ring or contains an R-regular sequence of length d [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence].

Every coefficient of phi_d is in the maximal ideal: apply the coordinate linear functional to the minimality image condition at degree d-1. Linear maps carry maximal-ideal multiples into maximal-ideal multiples, and the latter submodule of R is the maximal ideal itself. Reducing any last square submatrix modulo the maximal ideal therefore gives the zero matrix. Determinants [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant] commute with the quotient ring map (RingHom.map_det), and the zero matrix has zero determinant because n_d is positive. Hence every minor is in the maximal ideal, so I is contained in this proper ideal. This excludes I = R.

The other branch supplies a regular sequence rs of length d in I, hence in the maximal ideal. Unfold [def-weil-pbc-depth]. In the infinite-depth branch the desired inequality is automatic; otherwise the cast of rs.length belongs to the set whose supremum defines depth. Apply le_sSup and use rs.length=d to conclude.

The residue field is nonzero. ModuleCat.projectiveDimension_eq_of_hasProjectiveResolutionLE identifies its categorical projective dimension with d, using Nat.find_spec and Nat.find_min and the bounded-resolution bridge [lem-weil-pbc-projective-resolution-ext-degree]. Cast the proved bound d <= depth R into WithBot ENat. This is exactly the original finite-resolution dimension bound for the nonzero residue field.

lean.statement:
theorem residueField_projectiveDimension_le_depth
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    (h : ModuleCat.HasFiniteProjectiveDimension
      (ModuleCat.of R (IsLocalRing.ResidueField R))) :
    CategoryTheory.projectiveDimension (ModuleCat.of R (IsLocalRing.ResidueField R)) ≤
      ((IsLocalRing.depth (R := R) R : ℕ∞) : WithBot ℕ∞)
